prompt: Anamorphic 35mm cinematic split-screen diptych inside a data hall. A polished optical beam-splitter prism sits at the vertical seam on the concrete floor. A single warm beam enters from below and splits: left beam rises toward a fully populated rack row bathed in warm amber worklights; right beam flattens toward dim, partially empty racks in cold cobalt shadow. Brushed steel racks, graphite asphalt, bone white light. Shallow depth of field, teal-and-amber palette, film grain, no people, no text, no logos.
rationale: The article's governing tension is an interpretive divergence around a single number, not a physical machine; a cinematic split-screen still can stage two opposite readings in one data-hall environment with a beam-splitter as symbolic optical physics, preserving scale and editorial weight.
